title: worked on adding mobile shared session controls functionality to desktop UI
summary: In a shared reading session, the computer version now shows who's there the way the phone version already does. A row of participant avatars appears next to the reader's tools, and clicking it opens a **Participants** pop-up listing everyone with their role, an **Add friend** button, **Session settings** (host only) and **Share session**. The avatars on a session's tab in the sidebar can now be clicked too: they switch to that tab and open the same list.

links.label: Issue 2041: Desktop session participants: avatar stack in the reader and a participants modal

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the browser window at full width. Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old Seed Bible, do a hard refresh (**Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac).

setup.title: Get two accounts ready
setup.body: You'll play two people: a **host** who starts the session, and a **guest** who joins. The host must be signed in (Seed Bible emails you a code, so use an inbox you can check). For the guest, use a second browser, or a private/incognito window (**Ctrl+Shift+N** in Chrome or Edge, **Ctrl+Shift+P** in Firefox; **Cmd** instead of **Ctrl** on Mac). The **Add friend** tests need the guest signed in with a **different** email account that isn't already your friend.

setup.title: Start a shared session
setup.body: As the host, open **John 3** in a tab, click **Share**, then **Start and share session**. A link is copied to your clipboard. Paste it into the guest's browser or private window and open it, doing a hard refresh there once if the page looks old. Leave the guest signed out for now. Keep both windows side by side if you can.

sections.title: Avatars in the reader on a computer
sections.intro: The new avatar row sits next to the reader's tools (Save, Bookmark and the other tool buttons above the text).

tests.title: A shared session shows an avatar row next to the reader's tools
tests.why: Before this change, a computer only showed participants in the sidebar.
steps: In the host's window, look at the reader's tool buttons above the John 3 text.
Hover the mouse over the avatar row.
expected: A small row of overlapping round avatars appears beside the tool buttons, one for the host and one for the guest.
The host's avatar comes first and has an orange ring; the guest's avatar has a plain ring.
Hovering shows the tooltip `Participants` and a faint gray background behind the avatars.

tests.title: A tab that isn't a shared session shows no avatar row
steps: As the host, open a new tab with the **+** button in the sidebar and go to **Psalm 23**.
Look at the reader's tool buttons.
Switch back to the shared **John 3** tab.
expected: On Psalm 23 there is no avatar row next to the tools.
Back on John 3, the avatar row is there again.

tests.title: Clicking the avatar row opens the Participants pop-up
steps: As the host, on the John 3 session tab, click the avatar row next to the reader's tools.
expected: A pop-up titled **Participants** opens in the middle of the screen.
It lists the host first, labelled `Host`, then the guest.
Below the list, separated by a thin line, are **Session settings** and **Share session**, each with an arrow on the right.

tests.title: The avatar row works with the sidebar closed
tests.why: The issue's main complaint was that with the sidebar closed, there was no way to see who's in the session.
steps: Close the Participants pop-up.
Collapse the sidebar with the menu button at its top left (tooltip **Collapse sidebar**).
Click the avatar row next to the reader's tools.
expected: The avatar row is still visible with the sidebar collapsed.
Clicking it opens the same **Participants** pop-up.
Expand the sidebar again afterwards (tooltip **Expand sidebar**).

tests.title: More than three people collapse into a "+N" chip
tests.before: Open the session link in two more browsers or private windows, so there are at least 5 people in total (each new window counts as one person).
steps: In the host's window, look at the avatar row next to the reader's tools.
Click it.
expected: The row shows three avatars, with the host first, followed by a small chip like `+2` for the rest.
The Participants pop-up lists everyone, not just three.
When the extra windows are closed, the chip shrinks or disappears within a few seconds.

tests.title: Session settings appears for the host only
steps: As the host, open the Participants pop-up from the avatar row and click **Session settings**.
Close the Session settings window.
In the guest's window, click the avatar row next to the reader's tools.
expected: For the host, the Participants pop-up closes and the **Session settings** window opens in its place.
For the guest, the Participants pop-up shows the same list but only **Share session** below it, with no **Session settings** row.

tests.title: Share session opens the share flow
steps: As the guest, in the Participants pop-up, click **Share session**.
expected: The Participants pop-up closes and the session's share window opens, the same one the **Share** button opens for a session.
Its link, when copied and opened elsewhere, joins the same session.

tests.title: Add friend works from the pop-up
tests.before: In the guest's window, sign in with a second email account that isn't your friend yet, then rejoin the session with the link if signing in took you out of it.
steps: As the host, open the Participants pop-up from the avatar row.
Find the guest's row and click its **Add friend** button.
expected: The guest's row has an **Add friend** button; the host's own row does not.
After clicking, a confirmation like `Friend request sent.` appears and the button changes to show the request was sent.
In the guest's window, the request shows up under **Friends**.

tests.title: Signed-out guests get no Add friend button
steps: Open the session link in a fresh private window without signing in.
As the host, open the Participants pop-up.
expected: The signed-out person is listed, but their row has no **Add friend** button.

sections.title: Avatars on the session's tab in the sidebar
sections.intro: In the expanded sidebar, a shared session's tab has a strip of avatars under its name.

setup.title: Have a second tab selected
setup.body: As the host, make sure the sidebar is expanded and select the **Psalm 23** tab from earlier, so the John 3 session tab is **not** selected.

tests.title: Clicking a session tab's avatars switches to it and opens Participants
steps: In the sidebar, click directly on the avatars under the **John 3** session tab's name.
expected: The reader switches to John 3 (the session tab becomes the selected one).
The **Participants** pop-up opens, with the same contents as when opened from the reader's avatar row.
Hovering over the avatars first shows a faint gray background just around them.

tests.title: Clicking elsewhere on the tab only selects it
steps: Close the Participants pop-up and select the **Psalm 23** tab again.
Click the **John 3** tab's name.
Select Psalm 23 again, then click the empty space to the right of the avatars on the John 3 tab, within the avatar strip.
expected: Both times, the reader switches to John 3.
Neither click opens the Participants pop-up.

tests.title: Both avatar buttons work from the keyboard
steps: Click on an empty part of the reader page, then press **Tab** repeatedly until the focus outline lands on the avatar row next to the reader's tools. Press **Enter**.
Close the pop-up with **Esc**.
Keep pressing **Tab** (or **Shift+Tab**) until the focus outline lands on the avatars under the John 3 session tab in the sidebar. Press **Space**.
expected: Both avatar groups can be reached with Tab and show a visible focus outline.
Enter or Space opens the Participants pop-up each time.
Optional, if you use a screen reader: the reader's avatar row is read as `Participants`, and the tab's avatars as `Participants in John 3` followed by who's there, for example `… (Host)`.

setup.title: Use phone width
setup.body: Open the host's session on a phone, or narrow the browser window until the app switches to its phone layout (the sidebar disappears and a bar appears along the bottom).

tests.title: The phone participants sheet looks and works as before
tests.why: The list inside the phone sheet was rebuilt as a shared piece used by both phone and computer; it should look exactly the same.
steps: On the John 3 session, tap the avatar row in the reader's header at the top.
Tap **Share session**, then close the share window.
Tap the avatar row again and tap the dimmed area above the sheet.
expected: A sheet slides up from the bottom titled **Participants**, listing everyone with the host first and labelled `Host`, then **Session settings** (host only) and **Share session**.
It looks the same as on the main Seed Bible site.
Share session closes the sheet and opens the share window.
Tapping the dimmed area closes the sheet.

tests.title: Tapping a session tab's avatars in the tab list opens the sheet
tests.why: The intended phone behavior for the tab list isn't stated in the issue; the code opens the bottom sheet here.
steps: Open the tab list on the phone layout (the tabs/sidebar button in the app's menu).
Tap the avatars under the John 3 session tab's name.
expected: The app switches to the John 3 tab.
The Participants bottom sheet opens (not a pop-up in the middle of the screen).

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The Session settings window works as before
tests.why: Its code was moved to a new file in this PR, so it's worth checking nothing broke.
steps: As the host, on a computer, open the John 3 tab's options menu (⋮) in the sidebar and choose **Session settings**.
Turn **Only Host can navigate** on, then try changing the chapter in the guest's window.
Turn it off again.
Find the guest in the window's **Participants** section and use **Make co-host**.
expected: The window opens with its Participants section and settings, as before.
While the setting is on, the guest can't move the session to another chapter; once off, they can.
After **Make co-host**, the guest is labelled `Co-host` there, in the Participants pop-up, and their avatar in the reader's row gains an orange ring.

tests.title: Ending the session removes the avatars
steps: As the host, in **Session settings**, click **End session** and confirm if asked.
expected: The session tab closes for the host, and no avatar row is left next to the reader's tools.
No Participants or Session settings window is left open.

tests.title: Extension permission prompts and "crossed paths" names still read naturally
tests.why: A small helper that joins names into a sentence ("A, B and C") was moved and shared between these screens.
steps: Optional: if you know how to install an extension that asks for several permissions, install it and read the permission prompt.
Optional: on the **Today** pane, look at any row that lists several people's names together.
expected: Lists of items or names are joined naturally, like `your highlights, your notes and your camera` or `You and Jonah`, not with stray commas.

notCovered: The moving of the Session settings code into its own file is an internal tidy-up; it's only checked indirectly through the Session settings test.
The new automated tests added in this PR run on their own and need no manual checking.
